chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Abu Ismail al-Sarraj, from Ibn Muskan, from Thabit Abu Saeed, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Thabit! What is it with you and the people? Refrain from the people and do not invite anyone to your matter. By Allah, even if the inhabitants of the sky and the inhabitants of the earth were to gather together to misguide a servant whom Allah intends to guide, they would not have the capacity to do so.'

Refrain from the people, and not one of you should be saying, 'My brother', 'my cousin', and 'my neighbour'. For indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, when He intends goodness for a servant, He purifies his spirit, so he does not hear of a good act except that he recognizes it, nor of an evil deed except that he denies it. Then Allah casts a word into his heart by which He gathers his affairs.

key_terms.أَمْرِكُمْ: Your matter (referring to Wilayah or the Shia cause)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of refraining from inviting people to Wilayah according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In the era of political quietism, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) advised Thabit to practice 'kuff' (restraint) in da'wah to prevent the dilution of core beliefs amidst external pressures. He links this strategic reserve to the divine mechanism of 'tayyib al-ruh' (purification of the spirit), where God naturally instills intuitive recognition of truth and a unifying principle in the hearts of the elect, rendering forced persuasion unnecessary.
